The [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|Bruins]], led by seventh-year head coach [[Mick Cronin (basketball)|Mick Cronin]], played their [[home (sports)|home]] games at [[Pauley Pavilion]] as members of the [[Big Ten Conference]]. The Bruins finished the season 24–12, 13–7 in [[2025–26 Big Ten Conference men's basketball season|Big Ten play]] to finish a tie for seventh place.{{Cite web |title=2025-26 UCLA Bruins Men's Schedule and Results |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/schools/ucla/men/2026-schedule.html |access-date=2026-03-23 |website=College Basketball at Sports-Reference.com |language=en}} As the No. 6 seed in the [[2026 Big Ten men's basketball tournament|Big Ten tournament]], they defeated [[2025–26 Rutgers Scarlet Knights men's basketball team|Rutgers]]{{Cite web |title=UCLA 72-59 Rutgers (Mar 12, 2026) Game Recap |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401851378 |access-date=2026-03-23 |website=ESPN |language=en}} and [[2025–26 Michigan State Spartans men's basketball team|Michigan State]]{{Cite web |title=UCLA 88-84 Michigan State (Mar 13, 2026) Game Recap |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401851383 |access-date=2026-03-23 |website=ESPN |language=en}} before losing to [[2025–26 Purdue Boilermakers men's basketball team|Purdue]] in the semifinal. They received an at-large bid to the [[2026 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] as the No. 7 seed in the East region.{{Cite web |last=Los Angeles Times staff |first= |date=2026-03-15 |title=UCLA men's basketball earns No. 7 seed, to face No. 10 UCF in Philadelphia |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/articles/ucla-mens-basketball-earns-no-223730827.html |access-date=2026-03-23 |website=Yahoo Sports |language=en-US}} There they defeated [[2025–26 UCF Knights men's basketball team|UCF]]{{Cite web |title=UCLA 75-71 UCF (Mar 20, 2026) Game Recap |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401856496 |access-date=2026-03-23 |website=ESPN |language=en}} before losing to [[2025–26 UConn Huskies men's basketball team|UConn]] in the second round.{{Cite web |title=UConn 73-57 UCLA (Mar 22, 2026) Game Recap |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401856559 |access-date=2026-03-23 |website=ESPN |language=en}} The Bruins finished with a 17–1 record at home, including wins over top-10 ranked Purdue, [[2025–26 Illinois Fighting Illini men's basketball team|Illinois]] and [[2025–26 Nebraska Cornhuskers men's basketball team|Nebraska]].{{cite news|first=Steve|last=Galluzzo|title='Best we've played all year.' Trent Perry scores 20 points as UCLA routs No. 9 Nebraska|date=March 3, 2026|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/story/2026-03-03/trent-perry-ucla-nebraska|access-date=March 4, 2026}}{{cite news|title=UCLA beats No. 9 Nebraska, cruising 72-52 to snap the Cornhuskers’ 3-game streak|date=March 3, 2026|work=ESPN|agency=AP|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap/_/gameId/401825554|access-date=March 3, 2026}} In UCLA's opener in the Big Ten tournament, [[Donovan Dent]] had 12 points, 10 rebounds, and 12 assists in a 72–59 win over Rutgers.
